Hi Ellen / Aniket —

Thanks again for taking the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before scheduling a follow-up technical workshop. I copied Marissa (CS) and Connor (integration engineer) to keep everyone looped.

Call highlights (15 min):
- Goal: Replace heuristic ranking in NovaSearch with a neural reranker to improve precision at top results (improve conversion for product search).
- Primary constraints: 95th-percentile latency < 120ms for online reranking, max per-call candidate set ~50 items, sensitive PII in some doc fields (need encryption controls).
- Evaluation ask: compare current ranking vs Redwood reranker using your labeled test set; optimize top_k and reranker cutoff for production.

Open questions / asks from your side (we discussed on call):
1) SDK & auth: you prefer a short integration path (API key + SDK) for the PoC. For production you mentioned SSO/KMS.
2) Routing & fallbacks: you asked whether we can route to a cheaper model during peak and fallback to the high-quality reranker when latency budget allows.
3) Embeddings vs reranker: whether to embed+ANN filter then rerank, or run reranker over candidate set directly.

Mutual action plan (proposed):
- Today: I shared these notes and a small sample CSV with anonymized queries (attached).
- By Fri 07/03: NovaCorp to provide 1k labeled queries + candidate pools for 100 sample queries and desired KPIs (NDCG@5 target / MRR baseline).
- Week of 07/06: Technical workshop (45–60m) with NovaCorp eng + Redwood integration team to walk SDK setup, auth, routing policies, and run through a sample ranking job.
- Week of 07/13: PoC run: A/B evaluation over sample queries, generate NDCG@k/MRR slices, recommend top_k.

Attachments: postcall_notes.pdf (summary), sample_queries.csv (anonymized sample)

Next steps: Ellen / Aniket — can you confirm the dataset delivery timeline and whether the SRE team should be on the workshop invite? Also please indicate if the PoC needs to run on-prem (Private) due to compliance.

Hey Ellen / Aniket — Connor from Redwood infra team here. Quick answers and examples below. Happy to deep-dive in the workshop.

High-level: for most search flows we recommend two-stage retrieval:
1) Candidate generation: BM25 or embedding-based ANN to get a ~50 candidate set (fast, cheap)
2) Reranking: neural reranker that scores candidates and outputs a sorted list (higher compute but applied to small set)

We support both flows and can work with either your existing BM25 output or an ANN pre-filter. For ANN we can either: export embeddings from Redwood to your FAISS/Milvus cluster, or host the vector index in a managed service and hand back candidate ids.

Embedding dims / models:
- We support common embedding vector sizes (e.g., 256, 512, 1024) depending on model; if you want to bring your embeddings we accept arbitrary float vectors via the embeddings endpoint.
- Recommendation: start with 512-d vectors for general search, increase if you have domain-specific signal.

Ranking API (example request — pseudocode/curl):

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/rank -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"query":"wireless earbuds noise cancellation","candidates":[{"id":"p_421","text":"..."},{"id":"p_270","text":"..."}],"top_k":5,"model":"reranker-v1"}'

Responses include per-candidate scores; we return a deterministic ordering and a confidence score per item. If you prefer a two-step flow with embeddings we also accept candidate embeddings instead of text, e.g. candidates: [{"id":"p_421","embedding":[...]}].

Top_k tuning guidance:
- Run experiments for top_k in {1,3,5,10}. Primary metrics: NDCG@k, MRR, precision@1.
- Slice by query intent and length — tuned k can vary by slice (e.g., navigational queries favor smaller k).
- For latency-constrained apps, target top_k=3 and measure 95p latency. We can batch reranker calls where multiple independent queries arrive at once to improve throughput.

Metrics & eval tooling:
- We recommend evaluating NDCG@k and MRR over your labeled set, and also producing a per-query delta from baseline.
- For production monitoring we can emit per-route NDCG baselines and alert on regressions (Redwood Console integration).

Auth & deployment:
- PoC: API key via the SDK is simplest.
- Production: we support KMS/HSM-backed keys and VPC peering for Private deployments. We can provide SOC2+ encryption docs for your compliance team.

Attachments: I attached a small sample_queries.csv (sanitized) with 100 example queries and candidate pools to help the PoC.

Next step: propose 07/07 or 07/08 for the workshop (11:00–11:45 PDT). Let us know which is best.
